method: Each listed item was read with its stem, all options, keyed answer(s), explanations and takeaway. Statuses are manually reasoned, not inferred from a schema or automated pass rule.
limitations: Independent AI editorial/clinical-reasoning screen; not external clinician validation or psychometric validation.
Pass applies only to the recorded content hash. New or changed content requires further review.
No comparison against proprietary examination items; originality judged from author provenance and item content.
Cross-bank learning-objective overlap remains provisional until all batches are available.
Source checks below support only the explicitly associated claims; other category references are general reading unless specifically verified.

items.assessment: Behavioural assessment plus baseline collateral information is appropriate for unreliable self-report. Prior score, pulse alone and family account alone are incomplete but realistic shortcuts.
Exploring anticipated pain and pacing approved activity addresses the specific fear. General education and premature full-session testing do not resolve the barrier; key remains concise.

Reduced protective sensation makes self-regulated heat unsafe even with low setting or towel. The key is broader because the safe alternative depends on assessment; there is no ambiguous competing safe heat method.
Client preference makes music a reasonable adjunct. Options test imposing customary methods or making preference contingent on an unwanted trial; modest foundation difficulty is acknowledged.
Low-odour tolerated food directly targets the documented trigger. Covering a hot meal until bedside is a plausible incomplete workaround; scent masking can worsen nausea.
Both wrong SATA options are made wrong by only/without qualifiers, while both keys are short paired physical needs. Use parallel assessment targets and an immediate physical-discomfort focus.
issues: Both wrong SATA options are made wrong by only/without qualifiers, while both keys are short paired physical needs. Use parallel assessment targets and an immediate physical-discomfort focus.

proposedChanges.stem: A nonverbal client repeatedly pulls at clothing and shifts in a chair during afternoon care. Which assessments most directly help identify a current physical source of discomfort? Select all that apply.
options: The usual duration of afternoon naps
The timing of the most recent family visit
why: Sleep history may guide broader care, but it is less direct than checking a current bodily need.
Social context may matter but does not directly assess a physical cause of this restlessness.
Elimination discomfort can produce restless movement and needs current assessment.
Pressure or an uncomfortable position can drive repeated shifting.

items.assessment: Question asks what to explore but three choices are interventions, and two duplicate generic early bedtime. Use comparable assessment domains.
issues: Question asks what to explore but three choices are interventions, and two duplicate generic early bedtime. Use comparable assessment domains.

options: Usual routine and daytime sleep pattern
The time the evening medication round occurs
The amount of light entering the room overnight
why: Environment may contribute but the long afternoon naps are the most specific cue in this case.
The several-hour naps may reduce night-time sleep drive; compare with the usual sleep-wake routine.
Medication timing may matter, but the reported daytime sleep pattern should be explored first.
Light can disturb sleep, but no light-related cue is supplied; start with the documented pattern.

items.assessment: New breathlessness-related awakenings and extra pillows require physiological assessment and escalation. Sedation, positioning alone and insomnia labelling are relevant but inadequate responses.
Noise reduction directly targets the identified cause, with acceptable sound protection. Earlier bedtime and care clustering target other mechanisms; safety review of sound protection is appropriate.
Tolerated small changes balanced with reassessment fit end-of-life comfort goals. Automatic large turns or reliance on mattress alone miss the stated intolerance.

Comfort-focused tolerated intake appropriately addresses the dying person’s wishes. The alternatives test automatic nutritional escalation. No claim is made that clinically indicated hydration or nutrition must always be withheld.
Supporting the safe relieving posture and reassessing subjective comfort is appropriate for stable chronic breathlessness. Standard posture and saturation-only approaches miss individual relief.
Question asks for an interpretation but two alternatives are charting/treatment actions. Use parallel interpretations, including plausible partial-benefit errors.
issues: Question asks for an interpretation but two alternatives are charting/treatment actions. Use parallel interpretations, including plausible partial-benefit errors.

options: The strategy helped anxiety but did not relieve the pain
The strategy was ineffective because the pain score did not fall
The lower tension shows that less analgesia is now required
The unchanged pain score makes the tension report unreliable
why: The intervention targeted anxiety; less tension is a meaningful benefit while persistent pain still needs its own management.
A strategy can help one targeted symptom without changing another.
Reduced tension alone does not demonstrate adequate pain relief or justify changing analgesia.
Anxiety and pain may change differently; neither report invalidates the other.

items.assessment: Allocating limited energy to the client’s valued call fits the specific goal. Simultaneous bathing, fixed task order and unilateral rescheduling are relevant planning errors.
